outcomes.text: Students learn to apply AI methods to crime and justice questions.

courses.name: First Year Seminar
courses.description: Supports university transition, community connections and student planning.

category_review.locator: CS 1200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: University transition, resource use and personal planning fall outside the subject-matter categories; no programming content is established.

courses.name: Criminal Justice at Northeastern
courses.description: Introduces university resources, study practices and career paths associated with criminal justice.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The stated content is university orientation, study skills, services and career awareness rather than a substantive criminological method.

courses.name: First-Year Interdisciplinary Seminar
courses.description: Explores global citizenship, university resources and interdisciplinary problem solving.

category_review.locator: INPR 1000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The first-year seminar emphasizes university resources and personal/academic development with global-challenge context, without a sufficiently specified substantive subject for this taxonomy.

courses.name: Professional Development for Khoury Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op applications, interviews and workplace expectations.

category_review.locator: CS 1210 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Co-op preparation, resumes, interviews and workplace conduct do not establish a primary computing subject category.

courses.name: Professional Development for Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op searches, interviewing, professional practice and career decisions.

category_review.locator: EESH 2000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course develops co-op job-search, résumé, interviewing and career-management skills; professional preparation does not establish one of the substantive subject categories.

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Develops discrete structures, logic, proofs and counting methods for computing.

category_review.locator: CS 1800 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Sets, relations, induction, proof, logic and counting form discrete mathematical methods; computing motivates their use.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

category_review.locator: CS 2000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course teaches program construction, coding and introductory data processing to students without programming experience.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2001 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the introductory program-design course and practices its computing topics.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 2100 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Data/object-oriented design, data structures, abstraction, testing and software construction are the central methods.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2101 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the reviewed program-design and software-construction course.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 3200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Relational database design, query processing, indexing, concurrency and recovery are database-system methods.

courses.name: Advanced Programming with Data
courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3500 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Software architectures, reusable APIs, testing and maintainable data pipelines center on general software design and implementation.

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes linear algebra, probability and numerical mathematical foundations, using AI as their motivating application.

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
courses.description: Studies how to design, implement and evaluate visual representations of data.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Visualization combines programming, perception, visual communication and domain presentation; the description does not establish one defensible primary category among these.

courses.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
courses.description: Studies scalable data storage, distributed databases and retrieval methods.
courses.prerequisites: ( CS 3100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 310M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- ); CS 3200 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Distributed databases, storage architectures, reliability and data retrieval are computing infrastructure methods.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: DS 4400 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised learning, predictive models, model evaluation and learning algorithms are the explicit central content.

courses.name: Embedded Design: Enabling Robotics
courses.description: Combines digital design, programming and embedded systems to control robotic devices.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2140 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: EECE 2160 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description integrates digital hardware design, object-oriented programming/Linux and a robotic-device project without establishing one dominant subject among systems, programming and domain implementation. The robotics example does not establish an AI-method course.

courses.name: Fundamentals of Digital Design and Computer Organization
courses.description: Develops digital logic, computer architecture and hardware models for a simple processor.
courses.prerequisites: EECE 2160 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2310 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: EECE 2322 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Logic circuits, instruction-set architecture, processor construction, hardware-description languages and assembly interfaces establish computer architecture/digital systems as the primary subject.

courses.name: Lab for EECE 2322
courses.description: Designs, simulates and tests a computer system using programmable logic.

category_review.locator: EECE 2323 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The laboratory designs, implements, simulates and tests a computer system on programmable logic using a hardware-description language.

courses.name: Digital, Analytics, Technology, and Automation Research Practicum
courses.description: Applies analytics, digital technology and machine learning to client problems through a research practicum.

category_review.locator: MKTG 4606 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The practicum centers on solving client business/organizational problems with digital technology and analytics, combining technical and managerial practice. Machine learning is one stated tool, not evidence that a fixed AI algorithm curriculum dominates every project.

courses.name: Introduction to Criminal Justice
courses.description: Surveys U.S. criminal and juvenile justice institutions, their principal actors and the historical and contemporary effects of systemic inequality.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1100 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course analyzes criminal-justice institutions, actors, policies and systemic inequalities in the United States.

courses.name: Criminal Due Process
courses.description: Examines constitutional criminal procedure, police practices and wrongful conviction through case analysis and briefing.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1110 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Constitutional rights, criminal procedure and legal interpretation are the stated subject.

courses.name: Criminology
courses.description: Studies crime patterns, causal theories and measurement, including the influence of inequality and bias on criminological inquiry.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1120 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course develops criminological theories, crime causation and social responses with explicit attention to inequalities and bias.

courses.name: The Death Penalty
courses.description: Examines U.S. capital punishment historically and through constitutional disputes, innocence concerns, disparities, deterrence and other contemporary controversies.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1300 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Capital punishment is studied through history, constitutional decisions, public controversies and social inequalities.

courses.name: Human Trafficking
courses.description: Studies trafficking victims, perpetrator networks and the social conditions and justice responses surrounding sex and labor trafficking.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1400 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Human trafficking is examined through victims, networks and the social and cultural practices that enable exploitation.

courses.name: Corruption, Integrity, and Accountability
courses.description: Examines corruption through cases, legal frameworks, measurement and the roles of governments, businesses and civil society in accountability.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1500 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Corruption, governance, legal standards, accountability and ethics are the primary content; measurement examples do not make this a mathematical-method course.

courses.name: Crime, Media, and Politics
courses.description: Critically analyzes historical and contemporary representations of crime and justice in politics, news and entertainment.

category_review.locator: CRIM 1700 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course critiques political and media representations of crime and justice through historical and social analysis.

courses.name: Black Abolition Studies: Carcerality, Liberation, and Resistance
courses.description: Studies Black resistance to enslavement and carceral institutions through historical abolition movements and contemporary organizing.

category_review.locator: AFCS 3210 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Historical and contemporary Black abolition, political organizing and resistance to carceral institutions are the substantive social/political subject.

courses.name: Courts: The Third Branch of Government
courses.description: Studies judicial institutions, constitutional structure and relationships with other branches of government, including court visits.

category_review.locator: CRIM 2310 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Judicial organization, constitutional foundations and relations among government branches are the subject.

courses.name: Youth Crime and Justice
courses.description: Examines U.S. juvenile justice history and practice, including prevention, confinement, aftercare and disputes over bias and system design.

category_review.locator: CRIM 2320 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Juvenile justice policy, institutions, philosophies and inequities are analyzed in their social context.

courses.name: Punishment in the Age of Mass Incarceration
courses.description: Examines punishment and sentencing alongside prisons, jails, community corrections and the pressures of mass incarceration.

category_review.locator: CRIM 2330 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course examines punishment, sentencing and correctional institutions historically and in contemporary policy.

courses.name: Policing a Democratic Society
courses.description: Studies U.S. policing history, organizational culture, roles, research evidence and accountability.

category_review.locator: CRIM 2350 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Policing is analyzed as a social institution, including organizational culture, accountability, history and research.

courses.name: Restorative Justice: Transforming the System
courses.description: Examines restorative justice practices and their relationship to incarceration and systemic oppression using critical race and systems perspectives.

category_review.locator: CRIM 2370 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Restorative justice and penal institutions are examined using critical race and social systems theories; systems does not refer to computing infrastructure.

courses.name: Black Families and Incarceration
courses.description: Studies the historical and institutional effects of incarceration on Black families, parenthood and children.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: CRIM 2380 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course studies Black families in carceral institutions through historical, cultural and policy analysis.

courses.name: Criminal Violence
courses.description: Examines patterns and causes of violent crime and evaluates prevention, policing and punishment responses.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3010 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course examines causes, social patterns and criminal-justice responses to violence, integrating sociological and psychological perspectives.

courses.name: Global Criminology
courses.description: Compares definitions, causes and study of crime across cultures and examines national and transnational responses.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3030 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Cross-national definitions and responses to crime are studied in cultural and institutional context.

courses.name: Psychology of Crime
courses.description: Studies psychological processes and environmental influences on offending and their implications for prevention and desistance.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3040 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The primary focus is offenders cognitive, emotional, perceptual and physiological processes and their development, applied to prevention and desistance; this is psychological domain study.

courses.name: Organized Crime
courses.description: Examines organized crime’s origins, economic and political effects, links with legitimate institutions and policy responses.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3050 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Criminal enterprises and organized crime are examined through social, economic, political and legislative relationships.

courses.name: Political Crime and Terrorism
courses.description: Surveys political crime and terrorism, their historical and contemporary extent and efforts to prevent them.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3060 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Political crime and terrorism are studied historically and through contemporary prevention policies and information sources.

courses.name: Corporate and White-Collar Crime
courses.description: Studies corporate and white-collar crime, its measurement and causes, and responses from detection through sentencing.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3070 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Corporate offending is examined through criminal and regulatory institutions, definitions, case studies and causes.

courses.name: Criminal Law
courses.description: Analyzes criminal offenses, responsibility and sanctions through legal principles, complex factual scenarios and case briefing.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3100 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Criminal law, legal responsibility and constitutional, moral and public-policy reasoning are the core content.

courses.name: Substance Use and Social Justice
courses.description: Examines substance use through biological, psychological and social influences, emphasizing harm reduction, prevention and treatment.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3540 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description combines social-justice and oppression analysis with biological/psychological determinants and clinical prevention/treatment methods; it does not establish one dominant taxonomy subject.

courses.name: Gender, Crime, and Justice
courses.description: Examines gender in offending, victimization, criminological theory and criminal justice professions.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3110 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Gender and criminological theory are applied to offending, victimization and justice-system professions.

courses.name: Race, Crime, and Justice
courses.description: Examines relationships among race, crime and justice institutions, including patterns of offending and system responses.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3120 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course analyzes historical and theoretical relationships between race, offending and criminal-justice institutions.

courses.name: Criminal Justice Research Methods
courses.description: Develops and critiques research questions, methods and designs in criminology and criminal justice.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3600 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course teaches social-research questions, designs, critique and implementation for crime and justice, rather than a specified statistical or software-method curriculum.

courses.name: Senior Capstone Seminar
courses.description: Investigates a crime or justice-system problem and develops a policy proposal in a capstone project.

category_review.locator: CRIM 4949 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The capstone explicitly researches a crime/justice-system problem and proposes a policy solution grounded in institutions, law and criminological evidence; its subject is more specific than unspecified research.

courses.name: Analyzing and Using Data on Crime and Justice
courses.description: Applies statistical and computational methods, existing datasets and visualization to crime and justice questions.

category_review.locator: CRIM 3700 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The stated foundation is statistical techniques for social-science questions, quantitative evidence and visualization; crime datasets are the application context.

courses.name: Crime Prevention
courses.description: Evaluates developmental, situational and community approaches to crime prevention using theory and research.

category_review.locator: CRIM 4040 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Crime-prevention theories and policies are evaluated at individual and community levels using criminological research.

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops differentiation, its scientific applications, and introductory integration.

category_review.locator: MATH 1341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Limits, differentiation, integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus are the central content.

courses.name: Statistics for Economists
courses.description: Applies statistical inference, regression and data visualization to economic and social questions.
courses.prerequisites: (CS 1100 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MISM 2510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: ECON 2350 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Sampling, estimation, hypothesis tests and regression are statistical methods, with economics providing the data context.

courses.name: Issues in Race, Science, and Technology
courses.description: Examines how scientific and technological changes affect racialized communities and social inequality.

category_review.locator: AFCS 2600 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description examines social and racial impacts of computing, biological and physical technologies on communities; it does not teach those technologies as a technical curriculum.

courses.name: The Law, Ethics, and Policy of Data and Digital Technologies
courses.description: Examines legal and ethical rules governing digital data, privacy and automated systems.

category_review.locator: CY 4170 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description centers on legal rights, data ethics, privacy and the social impact of information practices, not security implementation.

courses.name: Cyberlaw: Privacy, Ethics, and Digital Rights
courses.description: Examines cybersecurity law, privacy, digital rights and information-security ethics.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2550 with a minimum grade of D- or CY 2550 with a minimum grade of D- or IA 5010 with a minimum grade of C- or CY 5010 with a minimum grade of C- or graduate program admission

category_review.locator: CY 5240 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course studies law, privacy, rights and criminal misuse surrounding information security rather than technical security mechanisms.

courses.name: Knowledge in a Digital World
courses.description: Examines how digital technologies shape knowledge and evaluates their effects through ethics and epistemology.

category_review.locator: DS 1300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Ethics and epistemology evaluate the societal effects of information technologies and policies; technology examples do not make this an AI-methods course.

courses.name: Knowledge in a Digital World
courses.description: Examines digital technology’s effects on knowledge through ethics and epistemology.

category_review.locator: PHIL 1300 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Epistemological and ethical frameworks evaluate information technologies and policies; mentioning machine learning does not establish AI-method instruction.

courses.name: History of Technology
courses.description: Surveys scientific and technological change and its relationships with society, culture and ethics.

category_review.locator: HIST 2220 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course studies the global historical development and circulation of science and technology in society, culture and ethics.

courses.name: Bostonography: The City through Data, Texts, Maps, and Networks
courses.description: Integrates computational methods with cultural and social research using Boston case studies.
courses.prerequisites: (( CS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- ); ( CS 2001 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 20LM (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )) or (( CS 2100 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- ); ( CS 2101 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 21LM (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )) or CS 2500 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or (DS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- ; DS 2001 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: INSH 2102 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Boston geographic, historical, literary, political and civic landscapes are analyzed through computational tools; those tools serve explicit cultural/social questions rather than a general software curriculum.

courses.name: Data Storytelling
courses.description: Develops data-journalism projects using analysis, visualization and tools for communicating quantitative evidence.

category_review.locator: JRNL 3700 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course explicitly emphasizes journalistic storytelling for broad public audiences, using quantitative analysis and visualization tools in service of communication.

courses.name: Technology and Human Values
courses.description: Examines technology’s social dimensions and ethical implications.

category_review.locator: PHIL 1145 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context

In these three courses, students have an opportunity to develop a foundational understanding of three related phenomena: why crime exists, how our criminal justice system responds to crime, and the constitutional and legal oversight of this process.

requirements.title: Conditional CSSH transfer-credit scope
requirements.summary: Apply these published CSSH guidelines only when the student’s college/advising and transfer circumstances make them applicable. CSSH participation in a combined major does not itself assign a home college.

requirements.title: Post-matriculation transfer petition
requirements.summary: Before outside registration, petition through the academic advisor for Provost review and keep the approved petition on file. Deficiency, unavailable relevant study or other permitted circumstances may support a request. A petition after enrollment/completion may not be approved; permission is not automatic.

requirements.title: Eligible transfer coursework
requirements.summary: Use an approved accredited institution, academic-credit coursework and grade C or higher; pass/fail and remedial, developmental, ESL, physical-education or nonacademic courses do not qualify. Credit awarded is no more than the originating institution’s course credit and can be less.

requirements.title: Transfer limits and finalization
requirements.summary: The page permits at most eighty credits from a four-year institution or sixty from a two-year institution, with a combined maximum of eighty. Finalize transfer credit within one semester after matriculation. Preserve these published scopes alongside any degree-specific residency rule; this is not permission for a particular transfer.

requirements.title: Evaluation and official records
requirements.summary: Obtain an official approved Northeastern evaluation before petition consideration; for an unlisted course provide its description and syllabus to the advisor for departmental evaluation. After completion submit the official transcript promptly, in an unopened sealed envelope or sent electronically directly to the advisor. Opened transcripts are not accepted.

requirements.title: Conditional CSSH graduation clearance
requirements.summary: If subject to CSSH graduation-clearance rules, meet the academic advisor in the junior year to plan remaining requirements; some departments additionally require a faculty-advisor meeting. The catalog’s Experiential Liberal Arts course requirement is limited to majors/combined majors entirely within CSSH and is not imposed on this verified Khoury/CSSH combination. Universal progression and degree requirements are already represented.

requirements.title: Conditional CSSH major-change process
requirements.summary: For a change into a CSSH major, meet the intended major’s academic advisor. F-1/J-1 students first submit the stated intent-to-change form. Meeting the faculty program director is strongly recommended, not mandatory. Students not meeting applicable entry/standing criteria may be denied, deferred until grades post or provisionally accepted. The page enumerates particular International Affairs combinations for its 2.500 entry/2.000–2.499 transition rule; it does not list AI and International Affairs, so those numeric criteria are not assigned to this degree.

requirements.title: Conditional CSSH dismissal appeal and re-entry
requirements.summary: For re-entry after dismissal to CSSH, submit its Academic Dismissal Appeal Form by the first day class offerings are posted for the intended return term, and arrange a CSSH advisor meeting for next steps. A first dismissal is appeal-eligible; additional dismissals may be appeal-eligible in some cases. Re-entry is not granted automatically. The page repeats university standing/probation thresholds, which are not added as duplicate degree obligations.
